name: Canaan
overview: Canaan is a male figure in Scripture, identified primarily as the son of Ham. He is notably marked by a curse pronounced by Noah, which sets him apart in the biblical narrative. No specific tribal affiliation or additional notes are provided beyond these key attributes.
namesAndTitles: The name Canaan means 'merchant' or 'trader,' reflecting a proper name given in the Hebrew text. This name is not indicated as divinely given but is recorded in Genesis 9:18.
familyAndRelationships: Canaan is explicitly recorded as the son of Ham. He is also the father of several descendants, including Sidon, Heth, Jebus, Amor, Girgash, Hivi, Ark, Sini, Arvad, Zemar, and Hamath, as detailed in Genesis chapters 10:15-18. These relationships establish Canaan as a patriarch of multiple peoples.
scriptureSignificance: Canaan's significance in Scripture arises from his position as the son of Ham and the recipient of Noah's curse, which has theological and historical implications in the biblical account. His numerous offspring listed in Genesis underscore his role as a progenitor of various nations, linking him to the broader narrative of the peoples descended from Noah's family after the flood.
